messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@alpinetech.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC plan & success criteria - Alpine Tech

Hi Jordan (and Connor),

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to hear more about Alpine Tech's evaluation goals. Per our conversation, I pulled together the proposed POC plan and a short list of success criteria to validate during the trial. Attached are: redwood-poc-sow.pdf (scope + responsibilities) and poc_success_criteria.xlsx (measurable criteria).

High-level recap / proposed plan:
- Objective: Validate Redwood Inference for production-quality NLU at 50k tokens/day with sub-200ms median token latency for priority routes.
- Success criteria (examples; see attachment for details):
  1) Throughput: sustain 10 concurrent inference streams at 200ms median token latency for 95% of requests
  2) Quality: model outputs meet the evaluation rubric (>= 85% on our prompt evaluation set)
  3) Integrations: seamless S3 ingestion and VPC peering for logs; no more than 2 security items to remediate by final readout
- Timeline: 4-week POC (kickoff week of Mar 22) with weekly check-ins and a final readout week of Apr 19. Detailed milestones below.
- Ownership: Marissa (project lead / commercial), Connor (technical lead), Jordan (customer executive sponsor), Priya (SRE lead), Alan (Security).

Proposed milestones:
- Week 0 (Mar 22): Kickoff, environment access, initial dataset validation
- Week 1 (Mar 29): Baseline runs, initial latency/throughput measurements, prompt collection
- Week 2 (Apr 5): Iteration on batching/quantization config, KV cache tests, quality evals
- Week 3 (Apr 12): Regression testing, production-like load test, prepare readout
- Final readout (week of Apr 19): Demo, metrics review, next steps (purchase/ Dedicated/Private options)

Immediate next steps I need from Alpine Tech:
- Confirm kickoff date (Mar 22 works on our side)
- Provide service account for S3 access and a list of sample datasets to run (CSV export is fine)
- Share any non-negotiable security controls that we should validate during the trial

I've also added a tentative HubSpot deal link and a DocuSign SOW link in the metadata for convenience.

Attachments: redwood-poc-sow.pdf, poc_success_criteria.xlsx

Thanks — happy to iterate on the criteria if you want different success metrics.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the quick recap and the materials. This looks sensible and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Security: Alan will run a quick review of the SOW; two hard requirements for us are (a) retention window controls for logs (ability to set to <30 days for trial) and (b) customer-managed KMS for key material. If those are covered in the SOW or can be done for the trial, that will speed approval.

2) Success metrics: we want to make "End-to-end response correctness" an explicit pass/fail metric — we've got a small labeled eval set (~200 prompts) that we'd like to run; target is >= 82% F1 for first-response correctness. The quality spreadsheet is helpful; can we add that metric as a row?

3) Timeline: Mar 22 kickoff is fine. Can we tentatively schedule weekly 30-min syncs on Tuesdays at 11am PT? That works best for our engineering team. Final readout Apr 19 is also OK.

Action items on our side: I'll loop Priya and Alan to grant the service account and S3 access by EOD Wed (Mar 17). Also copying our PM (Sylvia Park) — sylvia.park@alpinetech.com — for scheduling.

Jordan Miller
VP of ML Engineering
Alpine Tech

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Jordan / Marissa — quick follow-up from the technical side. Thanks for surfacing the KMS and retention asks — both are doable for the POC with the following pre-kickoff items from Alpine: 

Pre-kickoff checklist (Connor's items):
- Service account (AWS IAM) with s3:GetObject / s3:ListBucket for the dataset bucket; provide bucket ARN and a sample object path
- KMS key ARN and an IAM role for Redwood to use the key (we only need decrypt/encrypt for test keys during POC)
- VPC peering details or a public endpoint allowlist for our POC runner (we can run with allowlist for trial if peering is too heavy)
- Any IP ranges to add to the allowlist (if you prefer allowlist over peering)

Technical notes:
- We'll start with our standard 8-bit quantized model variant for initial latency testing and can switch to a larger variant if quality doesn't meet the F1 bar.
- For the labeled eval, please send the CSV in the following format: id,prompt,expected_label. Connor will run the eval and share the raw results ahead of the Week 2 sync.

I'll post a short doc to the HubSpot deal with these items and will also drop them into the kickoff invite so everything is collected. Looking forward to getting started on the 22nd.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Technical Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
